summary:
Tip: review of records access and transfers during the shift (2026-11-10, 10:25-10:35 UTC).

Supported findings (three, all kept by skeptic review):
1. Policy-violating transfer (F-8db130): workstation 10.20.1.21 sent 23,180,407 bytes to 10.20.9.62:8080 at 10:27:48-10:28:03. That destination is not an approved bulk destination and no change record covers it. It follows a 23 MB patients_full bulk export by account rhaddad from the same client IP at 10:26:38. Account used: rhaddad, in workstation session 54.
2. Forwarding stopped (F-ea24f6): adm-tkim ran "systemctl stop log-forwarder" on records at 10:30:50 within session records#402. The collector heartbeat from rec-srv-01 stops at 10:30:45 and resumes at 10:34:05. CHG-6914 (08:33-09:18) does not cover this.
3. Second-host session (F-0b669d): adm-tkim opened records#402 from 10.20.1.21, the nurse workstation, which is not a listed admin source (adm-lt-01 or vpn-gw-01). It ran 10:30:12-10:35:00 and overlapped rhaddad's workstation session.

Attribution: account use is established for rhaddad and adm-tkim. The human operator is not established for either account. Credentials at the shared console have been found written down before, and badge records do not cover remote sessions.

Not established: whether data reached 10.20.9.62 or was used; who typed the commands. Shell histories are not forwarded, so their gaps are notes only. The cache-0a91.bin mtime anomaly is host-writable metadata, unresolved. Auditor output was truncated, so other candidates (shell-history gap, records access.log gap) were not independently confirmed.
open_questions: Who was physically or remotely operating rhaddad session workstation#54 and adm-tkim session records#402?
What is 10.20.9.62 and did it receive and retain the 23 MB export?
Why was the log-forwarder stopped at 10:30:50, and was any change request raised?
Why does the cache-0a91.bin mtime (2026-10-11) predate its arrival (2026-11-10)? Is the workstation metadata reliable?
Do the rhaddad shell history and records access.log gaps reflect rotation, collection loss, or removal?
Were the truncated auditor candidates (shell-history gap, metadata changes) confirmed?
